title: E2E: SMTP session with daemon routing and header fallback
description:
End-to-end integration test covering both the daemon-up and daemon-down paths through a live SMTP session.

What: crates/smtp/tests/sieve_daemon_e2e.rs

Test 1 — daemon_up_routes_via_script:
1. Start sieve-daemon on a temp Unix socket using std::process::Command (or spawn the daemon in-process if architecture allows).
2. Configure smtp session with socket_path pointing to the daemon.
3. Upload a sieve script via admin API: 'require ["fileinto"]; fileinto "newsgroup:comp.test";'
4. Send a full SMTP DATA transaction (EHLO/MAIL FROM/RCPT TO/DATA/QUIT).
5. Assert: message appears in the NNTP queue under comp.test; 250 OK returned; INBOX is empty.

Test 2 — daemon_down_falls_back_to_list_id_header:
1. Configure smtp with a socket_path that does not exist (daemon not running).
2. Send SMTP transaction with message containing 'List-ID: Test List <test.lists.example.com>'.
3. Assert: message enqueued to newsgroup:test.lists.example.com; no SMTP error (250 OK); warn log emitted.

Test 3 — daemon_down_falls_back_to_newsgroups_header:
1. Same unreachable daemon config.
2. Send message with 'Newsgroups: comp.lang.rust'.
3. Assert: enqueued to newsgroup:comp.lang.rust.

Test 4 — daemon_down_no_relevant_headers_delivers_to_inbox:
1. Unreachable daemon, message with no newsgroup/list headers.
2. Assert: delivered to INBOX (Keep behaviour).

Oracle: NNTP queue contents and INBOX message count are checked directly via the same store APIs used in existing smtp integration tests.
